I've been watching lots of video recently (B2B SaaS obvs 💅). And most people lose me in the first 7 seconds.

I click anddddd: "Hi, I'm [name], [title] at [company]." Precious seconds spent on a business card read aloud. 🫠

We invented the title card. It does this whole job, while you talk about the actual thing. Your name can just sit there in the corner being useful context and building authority. 

We all talk about attention being a premium, how you've got seconds to hook someone... and then boom, the first 7 go to an intro that could've been an email. Sorry, a title card.

So why are we still verbally announcing ourselves? Is it trust? The algorithm? Some early-webinar-era instinct we never unlearned? Tell me 👇

"Maybe we could make a calculator."

Someone floated this in a GTM sync a few years back and I felt my soul leave my body.

Not because it was a bad idea. It was a great idea. 

It was a grind of an idea. Hunting down the right stats, building the right logic, somehow getting it onto the website, localizing it, making it mobile-responsive.

By the time we got there, I'd have filed for retirement.

So I just... did it myself. A few hours with Claude, a solid connector, and the specific kind of unhinged optimism that sometimes fuels me. 

The result: the ✨WISMO calculator✨. Mobile-friendly. Three languages.

WISMO ("Where is my order" for the ecom noobs) is one of the most expensive, embarrassing, and weirdly under-discussed problems in ecommerce (IMHO).

Customers asking where their stuff is accounts for a wild percentage of support volume. This calculator puts a number on it.

(I mean, don't you also dream of a world where you don't have to ask "Where the **** is my order?" anymore? 😂)

posts.content:
Walked in 100% certain content was the job. The whole job. Forever.

Today's my last day at Neople, and I'm leaving less certain about almost everything. And somehow more confident in what I can actually do.

Turns out professional resilience is just as much about riding the wild start-up rollercoaster as it is about holding two conflicting (and equally true!) things in your head at once.

That content as I knew it is dead, and content has never had more room to become something bigger. That AI made my skills replaceable, and made me harder to replace than I've ever been.

It's a state of perpetual dichotomy. Sounds like a crisis? To me, it's become a comfortably uncomfortable flow state fueled by curiosity.

A big ol' thank you is due: Bas, for the most generously human approach to AI I've met in this space, and for reminding me that the work that brings you joy is the only kind of work that's actually any good.

Job, for egging me into the weirdest, most wonderful corners of all of it to propel my character arc.

And Hans & Menno, for the trust, the transparency, and for setting a tone from the top that treated AI as a colleague, not a tool.

And thank you for the rest: Creating space for my AI side quests. Letting me get both a mascot suit and a bouncy castle. Hot dog day (and all its related fanfare). Somewhat patiently coaching my pronunciation of Webwinkel Vakdagen.

I've learned oodles. But most of all this: start with the safest endgame, and that's exactly where you'll end up.

So I'm walking out less certain than I walked in. Starting to think that's the upgrade. Certainty is comfortable. It's also where you'll plateau.

I've been digging through my own CV like a cold case and found a lead worth chasing: an industry I loved long before AI, but one AI is reshuffling now. Going back in to investigate, armed with two years of learned curiosity and zero chill.

And in the meantime: thank you, Neople. ❤️

posts.content:
It's official, I live in the AI bubble. 🙃

When I joined Neople just under a year ago, I'll be honest: I barely used any AI tools or even features within the tools I already used.

I was curious, sure. But the prospect kind of overwhelmed me. 

Even if they promised "efficiency" (or "money saved") as a ✨real person✨, these didn't really speak to me. 

SO much of the AI chat out there centered around doing things faster and not so much around doing things better.

Combined with the existential dread of being a marketing millennial in ChatGPT's "ever-changing landscape" (IYKYK 🤢) it was like I took a 4x double shot of espresso to my AI anxiety.

And the more I talk to people, the more I realize that there are a whole BUNCH of people who still fit in this category. (Hello, if this is you! 👋)

That's why I enlisted Seyna Diop to come break down all of the AI BS and hype for those who work outside of the AI bubble.

We want to have REAL conversations about AI that are 0% anxiety-inducing and maybe even a little funny.

First episode of our newest podcast, W(h)ine + AI, will be coming your way on Friday. 

Have a peep at the intro in the meantime in the comment section and subscribe if you want some down-to-earth, possibly slightly tipsy AI insights from the within the bubble 😉

Vinho Verde + arguing with Seyna Diop about whether or not AI is a reliable coworker or just a chaotic intern?

Sounds like the perfect Friday plan. 🍷

Sure, AI can summarize, brainstorm, even try to draft an email, but can it actually pull its weight like a real teammate? (Spoiler: sometimes yes. Often no. Occasionally, disastrously no).

Plus, you'll get to hear about my friend's weekend which was entirely planned by AI. 

Kick back with a glass and tune into the very first episode of W(h)ine + AI. You know where to find that link 😉

I went to The Growth Syndicate Con and all I got was this weird necklace from Louis Grenier. 😂

Kidding, of course, but you know it was a different kind of conference when you're taking away insights, a few observations you'll be applying at work the next day, AND a golden chicken necklace.

Most validating reminder of the day? Marketing is chaotic and messy. Embrace it.

Yes, you can try to science your way through dashboards and measure every touchpoint. But some of the magic comes from the messiness of humans. 

Be weirder. Be a little less predictable. And maybe start rocking a golden chicken necklace.
